title: Runtime: scheduler wiring, outbox sequence, smoke script in CI
story: As an operator I want the app to own its scheduler, give event consumers a per-tenant ordering sequence, and prove end to end boot in CI.
acceptance: createApp exposes ctx.scheduler (createScheduler from src/core/scheduler.mjs) and app.close() calls scheduler.stopAll(); tests/unit/core/scheduler-wiring.test.mjs proves a registered job stops firing after close

outbox has a per-tenant monotonically increasing integer seq column added by a new migration (existing migrations untouched) that backfills existing rows in created_at,rowid order; bus.outbox(tenantId) rows include seq in ascending order; tests/unit/core/outbox-sequence.test.mjs covers two tenants interleaving, backfill on a pre-populated DB, and no seq reuse after delivery

scripts/smoke.mjs boots the app the way npm start does on a free port (PORT=0 or discovered), polls /healthz, issues tokens, creates one claim through the HTTP API end to end, asserts the response, and exits non-zero with a message on any failure; tests/unit/core/smoke.test.mjs runs it as a child process and asserts exit 0
CI runs node scripts/smoke.mjs after the Test step in .github/workflows/ci.yml
All existing tests in tests/unit/core pass unchanged: node --test --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning tests/unit/core/*.test.mjs
brief: Read architecture/core-runtime-api.md and src/server.mjs, src/core/bus.mjs, scheduler.mjs, store.mjs, scripts/dev.mjs first. (1) Scheduler: in createApp, build createScheduler() and set ctx.scheduler before modules mount so modules can register jobs; in close() call stopAll() before server.close and db.close. (2) Outbox seq: add a new entry to bus.mjs migrations (do not edit prior SQL). SQLite cannot add a NOT NULL autoincrement per tenant, so ALTER TABLE outbox ADD COLUMN seq INTEGER, backfill with a window function (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tenant_id ORDER BY created_at, rowid)), create UNIQUE INDEX on (tenant_id, seq). On publish compute seq = COALESCE(MAX(seq),0)+1 for the tenant inside the same transaction as the insert (check how store.mjs does transactions and tenant scoping; the tenant-scope guard rejects unscoped SQL, so use ctx.db.forTenant(id)). Never reuse seq after rows are deleted or delivered: rows are not deleted today, keep it that way or document. Order outbox() and replay by seq. Keep the store scope guard happy; if it needs a tweak, make the smallest change and note it. Also honor pending security asks only if trivial; do not expand scope. (3) scripts/smoke.mjs: zero deps, use fetch. Look at scripts/dev.mjs and tests/unit/core/server.test.mjs for token issuance (/auth/token with devMode) and a claim create route. Prefer spawning `npm start` equivalent (node scripts/dev.mjs) with PORT set to a free port found by listening on port 0, wait up to 15s for /healthz, always kill the child in finally, and exit 1 with a clear message on failure. Use a temp DB path so no repo files are polluted. (4) Add a ci.yml step 'Smoke' running node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning scripts/smoke.mjs after Test. Pitfalls: unref timers, test must not leave handles open, do not edit package.json (add no npm script; call the file directly). Synthetic data only.
requirements: Per-tenant ordered event stream for consumers
CI proves the app boots and processes a claim

verdicts.reason: All 5 criteria met; core unit tests 42/42, smoke PASS exit 0, no new e2e/security regressions (openapi snapshot drift is from architecture's openapi.yaml change, not this ticket)
